title: Split a text message into segments a phone can show

blocks.text: The notification service sends long text messages as several SMS segments, and the phone joins them back together. A Unicode segment holds a fixed number of UTF-16 code units. Support has two complaints: some messages arrive with a `?` where an emoji should be, and the gateway rejects others as oversized.
`SmsSegments.segments(...)` already splits a message. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/SmsSegments.java`: `cut(text, units)` returns the index where the first segment of `text` ends.

When you're done, every segment fits the segment size, the segments joined give back the original text, and each segment can be shown on its own, whatever the message holds. About four lines in total.

cases.says: plain text is split into segments that each fill the segment size, the last one holding the rest
accented letters such as ü and ë take one unit each, so a text of them fills its segments fully
a text shorter than one segment is sent whole, as one segment
a segment never ends between the two halves of an emoji, so each segment can be shown on its own
the segment size counts UTF-16 units, so a segment of emoji holds half as many emoji as the size

origin.section: length(), charAt() and substring() Count UTF-16 Units, So an Emoji Counts Twice

concepts: length(), charAt() and substring() count UTF-16 units, so a character outside the BMP takes two and a cut at a unit index can split it.
